title: Host Genome-Metagenome Analyses Using Combinatorial Network Methods Reveal Key Metagenomic and Host Genetic Features for Methane Emission and Feed Efficiency in Cattle.
one_liner_zh: 该研究用组合网络和机器学习分析牛甲烷排放与瘤胃微生物组及宿主遗传关联，虽涉及转录因子GO注释，但核心是微生物组-宿主遗传关联，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Cattle production is one of the key contributors to global warming due to methane emission, which is a by-product of converting feed stuff into milk and meat for human consumption. Rumen hosts numerous microbial communities that are involved in the digestive process, leading to notable amounts of methane emission. The key factors underlying differences in methane emission between individual animals are due to, among other factors, both specific enrichments of certain microbial communities and host genetic factors that influence the microbial abundances. The detection of such factors involves various biostatistical and bioinformatics methods. In this study, our main objective was to reanalyze a publicly available data set using our proprietary Synomics Insights platform that is based on novel combinatorial network and machine learning methods to detect key metagenomic and host genetic features for methane emission and residual feed intake (RFI) in dairy cattle. The other objective was to compare the results with publicly available standard tools, such as those found in the microbiome bioinformatics platform QIIME2 and classic GWAS analysis. The data set used was publicly available and comprised 1,016 dairy cows with 16S short read sequencing data from two dairy cow breeds: Holstein and Nordic Reds. Host genomic data consisted of both 50 k and 150 k SNP arrays. Although several traits were analyzed by the original authors, here, we considered only methane emission as key phenotype for associating microbial communities and host genetic factors. The Synomics Insights platform is based on combinatorial methods that can identify taxa that are differentially abundant between animals showing high or low methane emission or RFI. Focusing exclusively on enriched taxa, for methane emission, the study identified 26 order-level taxa that combinatorial networks reported as significantly enriched either in high or low emitters. Additionally, a Z-test on proportions found 21/26 (81%) of these taxa were differentially enriched between high and low emitters (p value <.05). In particular, the phylum of Proteobacteria and the order Desulfovibrionales were found enriched in high emitters while the order Veillonellales was found to be more abundant in low emitters as previously reported for cattle (Wallace et al., 2015). In comparison, using the publicly available tool ANCOM only the order Methanosarcinales could be identified as differentially abundant between the two groups. We also investigated a link between host genome and rumen microbiome by applying our Synomics Insights platform and comparing it with an industry standard GWAS method. This resulted in the identification of genetic determinants in cows that are associated with changes in heritable components of the rumen microbiome. Only four key SNPs were found by both our platform and GWAS, whereas the Synomics Insights platform identified 1,290 significant SNPs that were not found by GWAS. Gene Ontology (GO) analysis found transcription factor as the dominant biological function. We estimated heritability of a core 73 taxa from the original set of 150 core order-level taxonomies and showed that some species are medium to highly heritable (0.25-0.62), paving the way for selective breeding of animals with desirable core microbiome characteristics. We identified a set of 113 key SNPs associated with >90% of these core heritable taxonomies. Finally, we have characterized a small set (<10) of SNPs strongly associated with key heritable bacterial orders with known role in methanogenesis, such as Desulfobacterales and Methanobacteriales.
abstract_zh: 养牛生产是全球变暖的主要贡献者之一，原因在于甲烷排放，这是将饲料转化为供人类消费的牛奶和肉类过程中的副产品。瘤胃内栖息着大量参与消化过程的微生物群落，导致显著的甲烷排放量。个体动物间甲烷排放差异的关键因素，除其他外，包括特定微生物群落的富集以及影响微生物丰度的宿主遗传因素。检测这些因素涉及多种生物统计学和生物信息学方法。在本研究中，我们的主要目标是使用我们专有的Synomics Insights平台重新分析一个公开可用的数据集，该平台基于新颖的组合网络和机器学习方法，以检测奶牛甲烷排放和剩余采食量（RFI）的关键宏基因组和宿主遗传特征。另一个目标是将结果与公开可用的标准工具进行比较，例如微生物组生物信息学平台QIIME2和经典全基因组关联分析（GWAS）。使用的数据集是公开的，包含1,016头奶牛，来自两个奶牛品种：荷斯坦牛和北欧红牛，并具有16S短读长测序数据。宿主基因组数据包括50k和150k SNP芯片。尽管原始作者分析了多个性状，但在此我们仅考虑甲烷排放作为关联微生物群落和宿主遗传因素的关键表型。Synomics Insights平台基于组合方法，能够识别高或低甲烷排放或RFI动物之间差异丰度的分类群。仅关注富集的分类群，对于甲烷排放，研究识别了26个目级分类群，组合网络报告这些分类群在高或低排放者中显著富集。此外，对比例进行的Z检验发现，21/26（81%）的这些分类群在高和低排放者之间差异富集（p值<.05）。特别是，变形菌门（Proteobacteria）和脱硫弧菌目（Desulfovibrionales）在高排放者中富集，而韦荣氏菌目（Veillonellales）在低排放者中更丰富，这与先前在牛中的报道一致（Wallace等人，2015年）。相比之下，使用公开可用的工具ANCOM，仅能识别甲烷八叠球菌目（Methanosarcinales）在两组之间差异丰度。我们还通过应用Synomics Insights平台并将其与行业标准GWAS方法进行比较，研究了宿主基因组与瘤胃微生物组之间的联系。这导致识别出与瘤胃微生物组可遗传组分变化相关的奶牛遗传决定因素。我们的平台和GWAS仅共同发现了四个关键SNP，而Synomics Insights平台识别了1,290个GWAS未发现的显著SNP。基因本体论（GO）分析发现转录因子是主要生物学功能。我们估计了原始150个核心目级分类群中73个核心分类群的遗传力，并显示一些物种具有中等至高遗传力（0.25-0.62），为选择具有理想核心微生物组特征的动物进行选择性育种铺平了道路。我们识别了一组113个关键SNP，与这些核心可遗传分类群的>90%相关。最后，我们表征了一小组（<10个）与已知在产甲烷过程中起作用的可遗传细菌目（如脱硫杆菌目（Desulfobacterales）和甲烷杆菌目（Methanobacteriales））强烈相关的SNP。
